newsitem.title: DUBAI: Oman exports rise 12pct in first seven months '96.
newsitem.headline: Oman exports rise 12pct in first seven months '96.

text.p: Oman's exports, mainly crude oil, rose to 1.5 billion rials ($3.9 billion) by July 1996 from 1.3 billion rials during the same period last year, Oman's official news agency (ONA) reported on Friday.

This was caused by an 11.9 percent increase in the price of crude oil exports -- to 1.19 billion rials in the first seven months of this year from 1.06 billion rials during the same period last year, it added.
Imports during the same period soared to 1.14 billion rials from 901 million rials -- mainly industrial products, food stuff, electrical appliances, animal feed, tobacco and textiles.

Non-oil exports, mainly dates, lemon, textiles and vegetable oil, fell to 102 million rials from 103 million rials in the first seven months of 1996 and 1995, added ONA quoting official figures issued by the development ministry
Re-exported goods, mainly food, tobacco and soft drinks, went up to 217 million rials from 176 million rials during the same period.

Oman, a major non-OPEC Gulf oil state, currently produces around 855,000 barrels of oil per day and relies heavily on crude oil and refined product exports as its major source of hard-currency revenue.
